dedupe_keys.name: evaluating grid resilience with growing data centre demand multi time step dc optimal power flow contingency analysis on an ieee 30 bus system du et al arxiv 2026

description: This preprint extends a validated multi-time-step DC optimal power flow framework to evaluate how aggregated data centre demand affects contingency-induced unserved energy. On an IEEE 30-bus system with flexible resources, a conventional load at a contingency-exposed bus is replaced with an energy-matched constant data centre load, and two capacity-growth levels are examined under generator derating, transmission line derating and coupled derating. Data centre capacity growth substantially raises system-level and data-centre-bus unserved energy under transmission-constrained contingencies: under coupled derating the high-growth case raises total unserved energy from 3.203 MWh to 22.891 MWh, and a supplementary coincident-demand case adds another 34.4%, so temporally concentrated demand amplifies resilience impacts even without more total energy. Producer: Yuhan Du, Erika Ardiles-Cruze and Javad Mohammadi, submitted 8 July 2026. Coverage: a test system, not a real grid. Access: free arXiv preprint; only the abstract page was read, and code availability was not confirmed. Licence and cost: free to read; licence CC-BY-SA-4.0 (the paper, as linked on its arXiv abstract page). Caveats: an 8-page conference paper on a small standard test system. Simulation uses: the framework shows how to test data centre load growth in power-system resilience and contingency studies. Related record: the AI data centre flexibility grid capacity expansion model (model-ai-data-centre-flexibility-grid-capacity-expansion-defer-shift).
